I have a concrete target now: `FileBackedOutputStream` and `TempFileCreator` in both `guava` and `android/guava`. The refactor will separate state-transition helpers from I/O operations, tighten the temp-file promotion flow, and clean up test coverage around the in-memory vs file-backed paths so the structure is easier to reason about without changing behavior.

item.text: I’ve found one concrete weakness in the current tests: close/write behavior is only asserted on the in-memory path, even though the implementation has a separate spill-to-file state transition. I’m refactoring the state helpers and expanding coverage for that file-backed branch so the structure and guarantees line up.

I’m editing the shared JVM and Android source copies now. The main change is to make `FileBackedOutputStream` validate before mutating state and to extract the spill/reset helpers so the in-memory and file-backed transitions are explicit instead of being interleaved.
The source refactor is in. I’m updating the tests next to cover both buffering modes explicitly and to lock in the new prevalidation guarantee so invalid writes can’t silently spill to disk.

item.text:
**Findings**
1. [`FileBackedOutputStream.write(byte[], int, int)`](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/G003_guava/guava/src/com/google/common/io/FileBackedOutputStream.java:207) validated bounds only indirectly, after state-transition logic had already run. An invalid write could therefore spill in-memory data to a temp file before throwing. I fixed that with an upfront `checkPositionIndexes(...)` and added a regression test in [`FileBackedOutputStreamTest`](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/G003_guava/guava-tests/test/com/google/common/io/FileBackedOutputStreamTest.java:148). The same change is mirrored in `android/guava`.

2. [`FileBackedOutputStream.State`](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/G003_guava/guava/src/com/google/common/io/FileBackedOutputStream.java:239) had reset, deletion, and spill-to-file transitions interleaved in a way that was harder to audit. I split that into `resetMemoryBuffer`, `deleteFileIfPresent`, and `promoteToFile`, which makes the in-memory/file-backed lifecycle much clearer without changing the external API.

3. [`TempFileCreator.pickSecureCreator()`](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/G003_guava/guava/src/com/google/common/io/TempFileCreator.java:66) and the ACL construction path mixed platform detection, reflection, and permission assembly in one flow. I separated NIO detection, Android version detection, current-user lookup, and ACL attribute creation into dedicated helpers. That refactor is also mirrored in `android/guava`.

I also tightened test structure in [`FileBackedOutputStreamTest`](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/G003_guava/guava-tests/test/com/google/common/io/FileBackedOutputStreamTest.java:128) by splitting close/write coverage into explicit in-memory and file-backed cases.
